content: A Task-Oriented SDS is typically designed according to a structured ontology, which defines what the system can talk about. In a system recommending restaurants the ontology defines those attributes of a restaurant that the user can choose, called informable slots (e.g. different food types, areas and price ranges), the attributes that the user can request, called requestable slots (e.g. phone number or address) and the restaurants that it has data about. An attribute is referred to as a slot and has a corresponding value. Together these are referred to as a slot-value pair (e.g. area=north).
